lectures.title: The Cron Daemon `crond` & Crontab Files: Editing and Permissions

cues.en: Let's now have an overview of how Cronjobs work so we get the cron daemon.
And the cron daemon is a service that runs in the background and it's a background process that manages
the scheduled task.
Because this is what we want to use cron jobs for, to be able to schedule tasks.
It executes those commands at pre-specified intervals and it will wake up every minute and check if
something needs to be executed.
It's named after the Greek word Chronos for time.
That's why it's called cron or cron, because it's the cron daemon.
And the way it works is that it reads in crontab files they're user specific files in var spool, cron
crontabs or on other operating systems.
For example, on a mac they might be in the folder var cron tabs, but those are the most common folders
for the user specific cron files, but we should never edit them directly.
Then there are also system wide cron jobs.
We can put them into the file e.t.c. crontab this file we can edit directly.
Please note this file must be owned by root and we must make sure that the group and others are not
allowed to write to that file.
So we must make sure that it's owned by root and only writable by root and not anybody else.
And then on Debian and Ubuntu systems, cron will also check the contents of UTC cron, but we should
not use this folder.
But if we have third party software they might just place a file in that folder and this file then will
be loaded as well.
But this is only on Debian system on and of course on ubuntu because ubuntu is based on Debian, but
